judged_text: The DB update commits before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, and a calendar-update failure throws a raw 500 after the guests are already persisted, so retries are impossible. Guests are inserted into the booking, but if the calendar update fails the caller gets an error; on retry the dedup filter finds the guests already in booking.attendees, uniqueGuests.length === 0, and the user gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of the calendar update being retried — the calendar is permanently out of sync with the booking and the operation reports failure for work that actually succeeded.

Guests are inserted into the booking, but if the calendar update fails the caller gets an error; on retry the dedup filter finds the guests already in booking.attendees, uniqueGuests.length === 0, and the user gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of the calendar update being retried — the calendar is permanently out of sync with the booking and the operation reports failure for work that actually succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is called with no error handling/transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error after guests have already been persisted. On a retry, the handler re-fetches the booking, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees`, and then `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, preventing retrying the calendar sync and leaving calendar/booking potentially out of sync. This behavior is directly implied by the control flow in the diff.
